title: Grid Microphysics to RAR — Model Data

A1.name: Bosonic statistics
A1.justification: Standard BE for non-interacting bosons; requires discrete, indistinguishable modes

A2.name: Gradient-coupled excitation energy
A2.equation: E(x) = hbar * omega_0 * sqrt(|nabla Phi(x)| / g*)
A2.justification: Node energy responds to local strain, not potential or density

lattice_derivation.setup: Two adjacent nodes i,j separated by l_g in field with acceleration g
robustness_analogies: Phonon dispersion in inhomogeneous elastic media
WKB approximation: turning-point frequency omega ~ sqrt(|V'|)

why_gradient_coupling.density_fails: m_eff ~ sqrt(G*rho); not function of g alone, wrong form
why_gradient_coupling.gradient_works: E ~ sqrt(g); produces BE form with one universal scale a0
why_gradient_coupling.conclusion: Only gradient coupling consistent with observed RAR universality

kt3_resolution.fix: Statistical occupation imposes local gradient scale
kt3_resolution.prediction: beta should recover 0.5 when Graph-AQUAL uses BE occupation

limitations.detail: Kinematic model only; no grid Hamiltonian or time evolution
No specific lattice structure, dimensionality, or spacing assumed
BE used as input, not derived from canonical quantisation
a0 is measured (SPARC), not predicted from grid parameters

falsification_conditions.condition: mu must be exact BE (not FD, Boltzmann, or power law)
Coupling variable must be g = |nabla Phi|
falsification_conditions.test: Evidence for rho- or Phi-dependent mu falsifies

falsification_conditions.condition: KT3 recovers beta=0.5 with statistical occupation

covariant_eft.role: Identified the gap (classical S gives wrong direction); established 5 structural results

relativistic_action.role: Cosmological perturbation theory (mu<1, Sigma>1, c_T=c); complementary to galactic regime

graph_aqual.role: Discrete solver; KT3 failure is the GRAV-sector manifestation of the same gap

this_paper.role: Bridges macro (EFT) and micro (grid) via gradient-coupled bosonic excitations
